capitals.name: Mumocheng (site unknown)

rulers.name: Dengshuzi

keyframe_review.note: 3.87 M km2 for 402-406 against the infobox 2.8 M km2 for 405 (ratio 1.38 of the infobox, within the factor of two). The shape is the khaganate's maximum extent from its first year (all of the Mongolian Plateau, Dzungaria, Turfan-Hami, the Hetao and part of Manchuria), although the page says the Rouran 'remained politically fragmented until 402' and dates the later conquests only for Gaochang (460); read it as the largest extent, not the extent at 402 (the Yujiulü Datan page, opened to date the early conquests, lists Datan's raids of 415-429 and names no land). Reviewer fix applied: the 699 Ordos cells are removed from 402, because the Rouran page puts a Wei offensive that 'drove the Rouran from the Ordos region' at the start of the conflict that followed the unification of 402; Cliopatria keeps the Ordos Rouran until 426 and drops it then with no event. [fx-23] Rewritten to the page's extent. The Cliopatria shape (3.87-3.96 M km2, 1.38 x the infobox's 2.8 M km2 for 405) adds Xinjiang (about 2,100 cells), Siberia (Tuva, Buryat, Chita: about 1,950), East Kazakhstan and Almaty (about 400) and Gansu, Ningxia, Hebei and Shanxi edges, none of which the Rouran page gives the Rouran before 460 (it says only that the Rouran 'remained politically fragmented until 402' and that their territory 'covered all of modern-day Mongolia and Inner Mongolia, as well as parts of Manchuria'). The rewritten extent is about 11,600 cells (2.9 M km2, 1.05 x the infobox). The Wei land (Cliopatria's Wei shape plus the Pingcheng and Shengle disks of the northern-wei dossier) is cut out: the page has the Rouran 'vassals (chen) by Tuoba Wei' and Wei attacks, not Rouran land inside the Wei core; Almaty belongs to the Yueban (see 460). The westward expansion is the ledger gain of 460.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria gives the Ordos (about 430 cells, 110,000 km2) to the Rouran from 426; it takes it away only for 410-425, where its Xia row sits. ledger.note: 402: Yujiulü Shelun proclaims himself Kaghan of the Rouran. Gaoche page: Shelun 'conquered most of the Gaoche tribes and proclaimed himself Kaghan of the Rouran on March 11, 402'; Rouran page: the Rouran 'remained politically fragmented until 402 AD when Shelun gained support of all the Rouran chieftains', regnal name Qiudoufa Khagan. Neither page names a seat, so the Mongolian Plateau is the researcher's reading. [fx-23] Region now the page's extent (the same as the 402 keyframe): the gazetteer's Mongolian Plateau differed from it by about 1,200 cells (the compiler had snapped 10,879 ledger cells to the 15,659 of the Cliopatria shape in 402).

union.text: the Northern Wei land of the northern-wei dossier (Cliopatria's Wei shape plus the Pingcheng and Shengle disks)

region.text: the Cliopatria 441 shape without the Ordos, Gaochang, Zhetysu and the Wei land: Dzungaria, the Tianshan, Tuva and the Siberian edge, the northern and western fringe

ledger.note: 460: the Rouran take the western and northern fringe that Cliopatria draws from 402. Rouran page: 'The Rouran expanded westward and defeated the neighboring Tiele people' (no year) and, in 460, 'subjugated the Ashina tribe residing around modern Turpan' and 'ousted the previous dynasty of Gaochang'. The page dates no expansion before 460, so Dzungaria, the Tianshan, Tuva and the Siberian edge of the Cliopatria shape are placed at 460, the first year the page dates a westward step (the year is the researcher's bridge; confidence 1). Zhetysu (Yueban), the Ordos, the Gaochang oasis and the Northern Wei land are excluded.

region.text: the Gaochang (Turfan) oasis, Kan Bozhou's kingdom

ledger.note: 460: the Rouran install a king at Gaochang. 'The Rouran subjugated the Ashina tribe residing around modern Turpan and resettled them in the Altai Mountains'; they ousted the previous Gaochang dynasty, the remnants of Northern Liang, and 'installed Kan Bozhou as king'. The page also says, undated, that the Rouran 'raided and subjugated oases and outposts, including Gaochang'. Gaochang page: Kan Bozhou's kingdom was 'a separate vassal kingdom of the Khaganate' and 'was dependent on Rouran backing', so the region is the oasis only (80 km round Gaochang, 70 cells) and is removed from the Rouran shape from 460 (keyframe 460); Hami and the rest of Turfan-Hami stay Rouran in the shape (no page mentions them).

region.text: the Gaochang (Turfan) oasis, Kan Bozhou's kingdom

ledger.note: 481: the Fufuluo (Gaoche) break the Rouran hold on Gaochang. Gaoche page: 'in 481 the Fufuluo began to interfere with the Gaochang and deposed one of their kings'; Gaochang page: the Gaoche king A-Fuzhiluo killed King Kan Shougui (Kan Bozhou's nephew, table 478-488?) and appointed Zhang Mengming as his vassal (table 488?-496), and the Qu dynasty from 501 pledged first to the Rouran, then 'had to submit to Gaoche overlordship'. The year 481 is the page's, that the deposed king was the Rouran client is the researcher's reading (confidence 2). The earlier date (479, from the Hephthalites page) is dropped: that page's 'In 479 they took the east end of the Tarim Basin, around the region of Turfan' is named by neither Gaochang nor Gaoche.

region.text: the Fufuluo (Gaoche) country northwest of Gaochang

ledger.note: 487: the Fufuluo (Gaoche) break away from the Rouran. A-Fuzhiluo, after quarrelling with Doulun, left with 'over 100,000 yurts' and founded a statelet 'northwest of Gaochang'; the Fufuluo were 'split between north and south at Dzungaria', and after Doulun's death in 492 'took several cities on the eastern route', cutting the Rouran off from the west. The Rouran page has the Uighur chief Abuzhiluo lead 'a 100 thousand tents' west under Doulun. Dzungaria is the researcher's reading of the statelet's land. Drawn out of the Rouran shape by the 487 keyframe (487-540).

541: Dzungaria back under the Rouran. Gaoche page: the Fufuluo suffered 'a series of defeats from Anagui before being annihilated in 541' (and the Rouran 'dispersed' them in 541); Yujiulü Anagui page: '541 ... This year he also ended the Gaoche threat'. The remnant (Tiele) rebelled in 546 and was defeated by Bumin 'at Dzungaria' (Gaoche page) while Anagui's bannerman Ashina Tumen 'suppressed a Tiele revolt against the Rouran' (Anagui page), which implies the Rouran held the country again. Neither page says what happened to the land in 541, so its return to the Rouran is the researcher's reading (confidence 2: the year and the victor are the pages'). Drawn in the Rouran shape again from 541 (keyframe 534, valid 541-545).

552: the Turks take the field against the Rouran. 'In 552, Bumin defeated Anagui and his forces north of Huaihuang'; Bumin 'declared himself Illig Khagan of the new Khaganate at Ötüken'. The Rouran page: Bumin 'quelled a Tiele revolt for the Rouran' and then declared independence after a dispute over a princess; Issik continued the attacks until 553.

555: the Rouran steppe falls. In 555 the Turks invaded and occupied the Rouran; Yujiulü Dengshuzi fled with about 3,000 soldiers towards Western Wei, which handed him over under pressure from Muqan Qaghan.

region.text: the whole Rouran shape of 546-554 as corrected here, without the Ordos and the Gaochang oasis

ledger.note: 555: the Rouran Khaganate ends. Infobox 'Disestablished 555'; the khaganate 'ended when they were defeated by a Göktürk rebellion'; Muqan annihilated them (those handed over, except children under sixteen, were killed) and the rest 'fled into China, were absorbed into the border guards, and disappeared as an entity'. Cliopatria's last shape is 554; the Göktürk shape begins in 555. Reviewer fix applied: the region no longer includes the Ordos (701 cells, Northern Wei's since 427-431) or the Gaochang oasis. About 1,963 cells of this region (Greater Manchuria 1,427, and an eastern strip of the Mongolian Plateau) lie outside Cliopatria's Göktürk 555 shape: the pages opened say nothing on who took them (the Rouran page lists Northern Qi and Northern Zhou in the infobox but names no land, and does not mention the Khitan in 555), so they go to no Cliopatria polity; the Turks' share is the intersect with the Göktürk 555 shape, as in identity.successors.

wars.name: Northern Wei campaigns against the Rouran
wars.outcome: A string of raids and counter-raids with no land held: Wei's 429 offensive scattered Datan's people, who fled; peace 431-436 with a marriage alliance in 434; further attacks in 438, 443 and 448-449, when 'Tuoba Na was able to inflict heavy losses on Rouran'.
wars.note: The Rouran page adds 424 (Rouran repulsed), 456 and 458 (Wei attacks, outcome silent), 492 (Xiaowen's 70,000 horsemen, outcome unrecorded, 'probably unsuccessful' per Kradin) and 525-527 (the Rouran serve Wei against rebels). Cliopatria's relation '(Alliance between Northern Wei and Rouran Khaganate) 402-533' is contradicted by these wars; only 431-436 and the marriage ties are peaceful.

wars.name: Rouran-Fufuluo wars
wars.outcome: The Fufuluo broke away in 487 and held Dzungaria against repeated Rouran attacks (508, 516, 520); they penetrated Rouran land in 521-524 but were repulsed.
wars.note: The pages disagree on 508: the Rouran page says the Tiele defeated the Rouran, the Gaoche page that Futu attacked and won but was killed by Mietu on the way back. In 516 Chounu defeated Mietu. The Hephthalites 'helped Mietu' and sheltered the Fufuluo (Gaoche page).

wars.name: Göktürk revolt against the Rouran
wars.outcome: Bumin crushed a Tiele revolt (546 or 551) and then broke with the Rouran; he beat Anagui in 552, the Turks occupied the Rouran in 555 and the khaganate was annihilated.
wars.note: Western Wei fought with Bumin in 552 and then handed Dengshuzi over; the Rouran 'allegedly attacked Western Wei with a million warriors' in 540.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; no treaty line is dated by the pages. The southern frontier with Northern Wei is approximate and the western edge (Dzungaria, Turfan) moved with the Fufuluo.

sources.title: Gaochang

No Hephthalites, no Hami.

sources.note: 541: 'This year he also ended the Gaoche threat'; 546: Ashina Tumen suppressed a Tiele revolt against the Rouran; 552 defeat. Silent on Dzungaria, Gaochang, Khitan and Xi.

notes: Cliopatria row Rouran Khaganate 402..554 (12 shapes). The row is a single 3.87 M km2 polygon with small clips: the 410-425 and 480 changes are overlaps with neighbours (Xia's Ordos, a Manchurian strip), not conquests. Corrected: the Ordos is removed from every shape from 426 (Xia, then Northern Wei; confidence 2); the end moves to 555 (page) from 554. Not settled: (1) when the Rouran held the Ordos, if ever (the Rouran page says Northern Wei drove them from it, undated); (2) the early extent: the page dates no expansion before 460, yet Cliopatria draws the maximum from 402; (3) Cliopatria's relation '(Alliance between Northern Wei and Rouran Khaganate) 402-533' is wrong or at best partial (wars in 424, 429, 438, 443, 449, 456, 458, 492; peace 431-436, marriage 434); (4) Turfan after 479: the Rouran page has a Rouran client king at Gaochang from 460, the Hephthalites page has the Hephthalites at Turfan from 479; (5) the Hephthalites were Rouran vassals 'until the beginning of the 5th century' (Rouran page) or split away 'in the early fifth century' (Hephthalites page); no ledger event, because they held no land of their own then. Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-gaochang (Kan Bozhou's regime, 460-640), fufuluo (the Gaoche statelet, 487-541/546), both states Cliopatria lacks. Kyrgyz, Khitan, Xi, Goguryeo, Buyeo and Tuyuhun: the Rouran page is silent. The Avar link is contested (page: 'many others contest this'; genetic data 'inconclusive'), so no successor is recorded for it. Page budget: five pages, all cited. [fx-23, 2026-11-01] The 402-459 keyframes and the found of 402 now follow the Rouran page's extent (Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, parts of Manchuria; infobox 2.8 M km2 for 405) instead of Cliopatria's 3.9 M km2 maximum, which is put in from 460 (new gain). From 460 to 540 the keyframes subtract Zhetysu (yueban dossier) and the Northern Wei core (northern-wei dossier). Pages: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rouran_Khaganate, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yueban.
